title: BOEING_2022_10K — Item 7 MD&A: 行业长期需求驱动与 GDP 假设（p23）
key_points: Boeing 称行业长期前景由经济增长、贸易与全球化带来的出行倾向提升等基本面驱动。
其 Commercial Market Outlook 以长期全球 GDP 年均增长 2.6% 为假设。
基于该假设，预测 20 年客运与货运流量增速 3.8%，约 41,170 架新飞机需求。
raw_excerpt: The long-term outlook for the industry remains positive due to the fundamental drivers of air travel demand: economic growth, increasing propensity to travel due to increased trade, globalization and improved airline services driven by liberalization of air traffic rights between countries. Our Commercial Market Outlook forecast projects a 3.8% growth rate for passenger and cargo traffic over a 20-year period. Based on long-term global economic growth projections of 2.6% in average annual gross domestic product, we project demand for approximately 41,170 new airplanes over the next 20 years.

title: BOEING_2022_10K — Item 7 MD&A: 行业对外生冲击的脆弱性（p23）
key_points: Boeing 明确列出行业易受燃料价格飙升、信贷市场冲击、恐怖袭击、自然灾害、冲突、流行病/大流行、环境监管收紧等外生因素影响。
该表述说明其周期暴露并非仅由 GDP 单一变量刻画。
raw_excerpt: The industry remains vulnerable to exogenous developments including fuel price spikes, credit market shocks, acts of terrorism, natural disasters, conflicts, epidemics, pandemics and increased global environmental regulations.

title: BOEING_2022_10K — 787 Program: delivery suspension, inventory, production rate (p35)
key_points: 787 deliveries were suspended from May 2021 until resumption in August 2022 (FAA authorization to resume received July 28, 2022).
Boeing delivered 31 787s in 2022; in 2021 it delivered 14 aircraft between March and May 2021 before deliveries were paused in May 2021 due to production quality issues.
Boeing stated it was 'currently producing at low rates' on the 787 and expected to 'gradually return to 5 per month in 2023'.
Approximately 100 787 aircraft were in inventory at 12/31/2022 versus approximately 110 at 12/31/2021; most 2022 year-end inventory was expected to deliver by end-2024.
Boeing adjusted its total estimate of 787 abnormal production costs up to $2.8 billion in Q4 2022, most to be incurred by end-2023 (vs ~$2 billion expected at 12/31/2021).
raw_excerpt: We received FAA authorization to resume delivery on July 28, 2022 and deliveries resumed in August. During 2022, we delivered 31 aircraft to customers. We continue to conduct inspections and rework on undelivered aircraft. During 2021, we delivered 14 aircraft between March and May 2021 prior to deliveries being paused in May 2021 due to production quality issues including in our supply chain. … At December 31, 2022, and 2021, we had approximately 100 and 110 aircraft in inventory. Most of the aircraft in inventory at December 31, 2022 are expected to deliver by the end of 2024. We are currently producing at low rates and expect to gradually return to 5 per month in 2023.

title: The Boeing Company Form 10-K for fiscal year ended December 31, 2022 — Competition / Commercial Airplanes business environment (p30)
key_points: Boeing describes facing "aggressive international competitors" intent on increasing market share, offering competitive products with access to most of the same customers and suppliers.
Airbus has historically invested heavily, with government support, to build a product family competing with Boeing's.
After acquiring a majority share of Bombardier's C Series (now A220) in 2018, Airbus continues to expand in the 100-150 seat transcontinental market.
COMAC delivered its first C919 aircraft in 2022; other competitors are at different phases of developing commercial jets.
70% of Commercial Airplanes' total backlog, in dollar terms, is with non-U.S. airlines.

They offer competitive products and have access to most of the same customers and suppliers. ... With government support, Airbus has historically invested heavily to create a family of products to compete with ours. After the acquisition of a majority share of Bombardier's C Series (now A220) in 2018, Airbus continues to expand in the 100-150 seat transcontinental market. Other competitors are also in different phases of developing commercial jet aircraft, including Commercial Aircraft Corporation of China, Ltd. (COMAC), which delivered its first C919 aircraft in 2022.

title: The Boeing Company Form 10-K FY2022 — Management statement on BDS and government services demand stability (p23)
key_points: Boeing states it continues to see stable demand at BDS, reflecting the role of its products and services in national security.
Boeing states the demand outlook for its government services business remains stable.
Boeing states commercial services volume at BGS recovered to pre-pandemic levels during 2022 and expects BGS commercial revenues to remain strong in future quarters.

title: The Boeing Company Form 10-K FY2022 — Commercial Market Outlook 20-year forecast (p23)
key_points: Boeing's Commercial Market Outlook projects a 3.8% growth rate for passenger and cargo traffic over a 20-year period.
Based on long-term global economic growth projections of 2.6% average annual GDP, Boeing projects demand for approximately 41,170 new airplanes over the next 20 years.

Boeing attributes the long-term positive outlook to economic growth, increasing propensity to travel due to increased trade, globalization and improved airline services driven by liberalization of air traffic rights.

In the same passage Boeing states the industry remains vulnerable to exogenous developments including fuel price spikes, credit market shocks, acts of terrorism, natural disasters, conflicts, epidemics, pandemics and increased global environmental regulations.
raw_excerpt: The long-term outlook for the industry remains positive due to the fundamental drivers of air travel demand: economic growth, increasing propensity to travel due to increased trade, globalization and improved airline services driven by liberalization of air traffic rights between countries. Our Commercial Market Outlook forecast projects a 3.8% growth rate for passenger and cargo traffic over a 20-year period. Based on long-term global economic growth projections of 2.6% in average annual gross domestic product, we project demand for approximately 41,170 new airplanes over the next 20 years. The industry remains vulnerable to exogenous developments including fuel price spikes, credit market shocks, acts of terrorism, natural disasters, conflicts, epidemics, pandemics and increased global environmental regulations.

title: The Boeing Company Form 10-K FY2022 — IATA airline industry profitability data cited in MD&A (p22)
key_points: According to IATA, airline industry net losses were $138 billion in 2020 and $42 billion in 2021.
IATA forecast $6.9 billion of industry-wide losses for 2022, with approximately $9.9 billion of profits in North America offset by losses in other regions.
For 2023, IATA forecast $4.6 billion in profits for the industry globally.
Boeing states airline financial performance, which influences demand for new capacity, has been adversely impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic.
raw_excerpt: Airline financial performance, which influences demand for new capacity, has been adversely impacted by the COVID-19 pandemic. According to the International Air Transport Association (IATA), net losses for the airline industry were $138 billion in 2020 and $42 billion in 2021. IATA also forecasts $6.9 billion of losses for the industry globally in 2022, with approximately $9.9 billion of profits in North America driven by the robust domestic market being more than offset by losses in other regions. For 2023, IATA is forecasting $4.6 billion in profits for the industry globally.

title: The Boeing Company Form 10-K FY2022 — 787 delivery suspension and customer contractual remedies (p9, p18)
key_points: Boeing experienced production quality issues, including in its supply chain, contributing to lower 787 deliveries, including a suspension of 787 deliveries from May 2021 to August 2022.
A number of customers have contractual remedies, including compensation for late deliveries or rights to reject individual airplane deliveries based on delivery delays.

Delays on the 737, 777X and 787 programs have resulted in, and may continue to result in, customers having the right to terminate orders, be compensated for late deliveries and/or substitute orders for other Boeing aircraft.

title: The Boeing Company Form 10-K FY2022 — Debt load, maturities and financing commitments (p18, p47)

Airplane financing commitments totaled $16.1 billion at December 31, 2022.

Boeing states its debt balances increased significantly since 2019, driven primarily by the 737 MAX grounding and the COVID-19 pandemic, and that the increased debt balance resulted in credit rating downgrades in 2020.
raw_excerpt: We depend, in part, upon the issuance of debt to fund our operations and contractual commitments. As of December 31, 2022, our debt totaled $57.0 billion of which approximately $14.5 billion of principal payments on outstanding debt will become due over the next three years. In addition, as of December 31, 2022, our airplane financing commitments totaled $16.1 billion. Our increased debt balance resulted in downgrades to our credit ratings in 2020, and our ratings remained unchanged in 2022 and 2021.
